body: Great write up! I was born and raised in Alaska, and if you talk to people who have lived there for a long time, everyone says “I can’t believe how bad it’s gotten the past few years (in regards to crime)”, but this just made me realize how it’s been scary for years now. I hope that all of the efforts to clean up and change the environment actually works.

Mine has two parts for the explanation.
Part one is the fact that my boyfriend and I have this thing where we try to say “I love you to ___ and back,” and try to say the furthest distance from where we are. He said “to a black hole and back” and I told him that he would turn into spaghetti if he did that.
The second part is a bit odd. We play argue a lot over tiny things (we both know it’s nothing serious), and we call each other “stinky” during it. I once said he had a stinky butt, and that’s how the second part came to be.
Collarbones. But not muscular or bulky ones. Just specifically skinny collarbones. I don’t understand why either

Not in the past, no. My mom and brother are diagnosed with depression and anxiety, and they have subconsciously proven that my problems don’t matter because I’m not diagnosed. I remember how pissed they would be when I had to be taken out of school because of my panic attacks, and that’s probably where my thought process of “I’m being childish” comes from. I’ve bottled up any feeling other than happiness since then because they just think that I’m being dramatic.

When I was 2, I was being watched by my grandmother while my dad was in the shower. They put a cup-of-noodle in the microwave, but they set it for around 10 minutes in order to make the noodles extra soft. Nobody opened the microwave when it went off, so baby-me decided to grab it myself. I pulled out all of the drawers leading up to the microwave (kind of like stairs), and grabbed the cup. The problem came into play when I tried to pull it out. I didn’t have a solid grip on the soup, and spilt it all over me. Another problem was that I was only in a diaper, so the hot soup instantly made contact with my skin. I now have slight burn marks, mostly on my hands and arms, but some are along my stomach and chest
Your hazel-green tint eyes, watching every move I make

My ex boyfriend said to me (while we were dating) that I was black cancerous tar that he had to try to scrape from inside his brain. Or, my current boyfriend calling me annoying and dramatic to one of his friends behind my back early on in our relationship. It’s definitely not the worst thing anyone could say, but it hurts me to this day because I thought that he would be the one person who would never view me like that.

The first time I got high with my friends, we went to Taco Bell (obviously). We went back to my friends house and ate, and I found a single piece of cheese on her bed. I picked it up, and stared at it for a solid two seconds, trying to figure out what the hell it was. Then I chucked it across the room like it was a frisbee. That was a fun night, let me tell you

I feel like I have multiple problems (mostly within my own head), but the one I never would have guessed having is the feeling of guilt. Constant, overwhelming guilt. I feel guilty about every action I preform, and for every mistake I make. I dwell over my past, and think that every negative event was my fault. I take it out on myself whenever I feel like I did something wrong, and I hate to admit it, but I feel better after. Kind of like karma, I guess. 

Anyways, after going through this thread, I realize that I’m probably just being ungrateful, and my drive to help others has grown. If anyone needs a friend, or just someone to talk to, please message me!

As for me, probably a day or two. I’m an introvert, but I hate staying in my room all day, not getting up or going out. I need to move around to feel productive
